# When Everything Goes Wrong, That’s When You Go Right

### Your Wednesday VC Breakfast Rundown

Jesse Landry

Dec 03, 2025

Share

Murphy’s Law may sound fatalistic, but Super Thinking frames it as one of the most practical tools a founder can have. Anything that can go wrong, will isn’t a warning to panic, it’s an invitation to prepare. The founders in today’s rundown embody that mindset. They build like realists and execute like optimists. They assume problems will surface, so they design products, teams, and processes that can withstand shock without losing momentum.Instead of fearing breakdowns, they budget for them. Instead of hoping talent works out, they structure accountability. Instead of trusting the market to behave, they build flexibility into their model. These are founders who don’t just survive volatility, they are sharpened by it. They’ve learned that setbacks aren’t setbacks unless you’re unprepared. When you engineer resilience, chaos becomes just another input.That’s the through-line of today’s companies: adaptability, durability, and a refusal to be blindsided. They demonstrate that great startups don’t succeed because nothing goes wrong, they succeed because they’re strong enough to move forward when everything does.
